items.title: Internal irregularities discovered in the Middle East & Africa region, essentially within the 'Government Services' sub-segment (audits/inspections for public-sector accounts) - discovered following internal whistleblower alerts, self-reported to the French authorities as a voluntary transparency step.
items.allegedBy: The Company's own internal checks, French authorities informed voluntarily (exact nature - corruption, falsification - not publicly specified; one analyst explicitly asked whether this amounted to corruption on the Q1 2026 call without a clear-cut answer from management)
items.outcome: Contracts concerned terminated, full exit from the Government Services sub-segment initiated in Q2 2026 and set to continue throughout 2026 (a few contracts may run into early 2027). Provision of 32,0 M€ booked at 30/06/2026 representing the best estimate to date of the financial consequences. Stock -13% on the day of the initial announcement (April 2026).

hypothese.summary: Solid H1 2026: organic growth 5,0% (accelerating to 5,5% in Q2), adjusted operating margin 15,5% (+29bp at constant FX), FY2026 guidance RAISED (organic growth 'mid-to-high single-digit' against 'mid single-digit'). The Government Services compliance matter (April 2026) is now QUANTIFIED: provision of 32,0 M€ booked, exit from the sub-segment under way, event described as 'clarifying' by brokers. Adjusted net debt sharply higher at 1 688,6 M€ (dividend timing effect, Q2 vs Q3 last year, within the LEAP 28 range of 1,0-2,0x EBITDA at 1,45x). O&P/Coal disposal signed (470 M€ EV, closing targeted Q1 2027) and LotusWorks acquisition completed (data centres/semiconductors). Normalised omniumEPS 1,42->2,25 (2026-2030), revised down in the near term (compliance charge now actual, revenue base reduced by portfolio rotation) but convergence virtually unchanged out to 2029-2030.
hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
H1 2026 confirms the TIC compounder mechanics: organic +5.0% accelerating to +5.5% in Q2, adjusted margin +29bp at constant FX, and the FY26 growth guidance RAISED to moderate-to-high single digit (net of engaged disposals). The market rewarded the print (+7-8%) despite lower absolute revenue from portfolio pruning. The refresh integrates the Government-Services compliance charge into the normalized base - the main reason Omnium 2026 EPS (1.42) sits below the pre-publication consensus (1.53-1.58).

== THESIS READ ==
- Organic acceleration plus margin expansion is exactly the LEAP28-style algorithm the thesis prices. Watch: Q3 organic print against stiffer comps.
- Portfolio pruning (disposals) trims reported revenue but raises mix quality - the guidance raise is expressed NET of it. Watch: disposal proceeds redeployment (bolt-ons).
- The compliance dossier is a contained one-off in the model, not a franchise issue. Watch: any follow-on provisions at FY26.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
Base = adjusted IFRS with acquisition-intangible amortization KEPT (serial bolt-on acquirer, E5) - structurally below broker adjusted figures. Semi-annual P&L cadence (semester split added per E5 ter). Qualitative guider: the scorecard anchors on the BV-compiled consensus by necessity (documented).

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
FY26 bottom-up: H1 normalized actual (EBIT 483.1M, margin 14.83%, EPS 0.647) + H2 on guidance/margin trend. ETR 29.3% (real H1 adjusted rate); minorities ~-25M; finNet declining with deleveraging (1,490 -> 400M). 2027-2030: ~5%/yr organic + bolt-ons, margin +30-40bp/yr, shares -1%/yr. Watch: compliance dossier tail; FX drag; consensus reset post-charge.

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 revenue (Oct); FY26 results (Feb 2027); bolt-on M&A cadence; margin milestone toward 16.5%.

hypothese.guidanceLongTerme: LEAP | 28 (announced March 2024, reaffirmed): high-single-digit total revenue growth (mid-to-high single-digit organic + M&A/portfolio rotation); continuous improvement in the adjusted operating margin (~17% targeted for 2028); double-digit annual return (EPS growth + dividend yield) at constant FX over 2024-2028; cash conversion above 90%; dividend = 65% of adjusted net income; target net leverage ratio 1,0x-2,0x by 2028.

epsReported.note: Adjusted EPS EUR 0.68 (+9.8% cc) is the headline metric; reported (IFRS) EPS not restated here - includes the EUR 32M Government Services compliance provision and portfolio-exit effects. To be anchored from the H1 report at next refresh.

dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: No specific quantified quarterly guidance (the Group guides on organic growth/margin for the full year); next milestone = Q3 2026 revenue on 21/10/26.
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: FY2026: mid-to-high single-digit organic growth (raised); adjusted operating margin improving at constant FX; cash flow at a high level.
pointsCles: H1 organic growth of 5.0% with a sequential acceleration to +5.5% in Q2 (Q1 +4.5%), led by Buildings & Infrastructure (+8.7%, Q2 +10.2%; data-center QA/QC and commissioning >+40% on hyperscaler capex) and Marine & Offshore (+8.7%); adjusted operating margin 15.5% (+29bp at constant FX, of which +22bp from portfolio scope) and adjusted EPS +9.8% cc (EUR 0.68).

The structural event: the ~20% portfolio-rotation milestone (vs 2023 base) was reached in H1 - Oil & Petrochemicals + Coal divestment signed (~$450M of 2025 revenue, EV $470M, ~11x EBIT), legacy Government Services exit nearly complete by year-end, 5 acquisitions YTD (~EUR 138M revenue incl. LotusWorks in mission-critical assets) - and reporting moves from 6 to 4 divisions on July 1 with both exits treated as IFRS discontinued operations from Q3 (restated comparables to come).

FY26 guidance UPGRADED on the new perimeter: mid-to-high single-digit organic growth (based on performance, pipeline and backlog - explicitly NOT assuming a Middle East rebound), continued margin improvement at constant FX and high cash generation; the Government Services compliance file is now ring-fenced (review complete, authorities informed, EUR 32M provision = best estimate of the FULL financial impact).

Watch items: Certification underperformed (+1.9%, execution shortfall in mature-market QHSE - CEO 'not pleased', sales/operations reviews launched with H2 pickup promised) while transition services and digital assurance grew high single digit; FX headwind fading fast (-5.2% Q1 -> -0.6% Q2, June slightly accretive); CMD on 22 September in Paris (next LEAP | 28 phase incl. a full AI update); Q3 print 21 October on the new reporting.

ancrages.moteur: The Government Services compliance matter, not quantified at the creation of the thesis (Q1 2026), is now quantified: provision of 32,0 M€ booked at 30/06/26, already excluded from adjusted operating income (like the other non-recurring items in H1, 32,9 M€ in total) -> reintegrated as a genuine one-off in the normalised H1 2026 build (does not affect the 2027+ trajectory, the exit from the sub-segment being virtually complete by end-2026).

FY2026 guidance raised from 'mid single-digit' to 'mid-to-high single-digit' organic growth, with sequential acceleration already observed Q1->Q2 (4,5%->5,5%) -> H2 2026 revenue trajectory built with organic growth close to the high end of the range, tempered by the dilutive effect of the progressive exit from Government Services.

Signed disposal of the Oil & Petrochemicals Products and Coal businesses (enterprise value 470 M€, ~450 M€ of annualised 2025 revenue, closing targeted for end-Q1 2027) -> cuts the 2027 revenue base by about 450 M€ (businesses with below-Group-average growth and margin, hence an accretive impact on the margin despite the loss of absolute revenue), with the disposal proceeds redeployed towards higher-growth/higher-margin M&A in line with LEAP 28.

Adjusted net financial debt at 1 688,6 M€ as at 30/06/26 (vs 1 253,3 M€ at end-2025) driven essentially by the timing shift in the dividend payment (427,7 M€ paid in Q2 26 versus Q3 25 last year) rather than by any operating deterioration -> 2026 omniumND trajectory raised vs the creation thesis (starting base higher than projected), with deleveraging thereafter carried by recurring FCF and the proceeds of the O&P/Coal disposal in 2027.

Amortisation of intangible assets arising from acquisitions (23,4 M€ in H1 26, consistent with the historical run-rate) retained in the normalised base as it is recurring at a serial acquirer such as Bureau Veritas - methodology unchanged since the creation thesis.

Adjusted effective tax rate maintained at 29,3% (consistent with the actual H1 26 adjusted ETR of 29,3%, stable vs 29,2% in H1 25 despite the French exceptional contribution booked in full in H1 - a timing effect rather than a structural increase in the rate).

LEAP 28 ambition reaffirmed of an adjusted operating margin close to 17% in 2028, with the CFO indicating a wish to get there 'without significant annual fluctuation' -> normalised margin trajectory built as a gradual, steady progression from 15,6% (2026) to ~17,6% (2030), rather than an abrupt jump in a given year.

The CFO explicitly confirms (Q&A, reply to Jefferies) that the +22bp favourable scope effect on the H1 margin is NOT linked to the Government Services/food testing disposals and is 'here to stay through the year' on the end-June scope -> margin tailwind treated as structurally secured for the remainder of the year (excluding new acquisitions/disposals), supporting the H2 2026 margin trajectory without assuming an exceptional rebound.
